response.sql: WITH oc AS (SELECT account_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM "order" GROUP BY account_id), avg_all AS (SELECT AVG(cnt) AS avg_cnt FROM oc), above AS (SELECT oc.account_id, oc.cnt FROM oc, avg_all WHERE oc.cnt > avg_all.avg_cnt), above_avg AS (SELECT AVG(cnt) AS kept_avg FROM above) SELECT a.account_id, a.cnt AS order_count, a.cnt - av.avg_cnt AS diff_from_avg, a.cnt - ab.kept_avg AS diff_from_kept_avg FROM above a, avg_all av, above_avg ab ORDER BY diff_from_kept_avg DESC, a.account_id LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: Each row in the "order" table is one standing order, so the order count per account is COUNT(*) over that table; accounts with no rows are excluded from the average, as the request specifies.

The average over accounts is the mean of per-account order counts (not the mean of orders weighted some other way), and the second average is the mean of the counts of the accounts kept as above average.
